newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-RAVENS AGREE TO TERMS WITH FREE AGENT TACKLE SIRAGUSA.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-RAVENS AGREE TO TERMS WITH FREE AGENT TACKLE SIRAGUSA.

text.p: The Baltimore Ravens agreed to terms with free agent defensive tackle Tony Siragusa on Thursday, reuniting him with former Indianapolis Colts head coach Ted Marchibroda.
Terms were not disclosed, but the Indianapolis Star reported that Siragusa was signing a four-year deal worth approximately $6.1 million.

The 6-3 (1.91 m), 330-pound (150 kg) Siragusa, who turns 30 next month, has played all seven of his NFL seasons with the Colts. He had his best season in 1994 with career highs in tackles (108), sacks (five) and forced fumbles (three).

"Goose (Siragusa) is an outstanding addition," said Marchibroda. "He is a run-stopping impact player, and he's a personality. He'll bring some leadership and some character to the locker room. We need that."

Siragusa, however, was on the field just 35 percent of the time last year due to injury and was often replaced on passing downs. He needed arthroscopic surgery to repair damage to his right knee late last year.
Marchibroda was head coach of the Colts from 1992 to 1995.

Baltimore has been intent on improving its defence. The Ravens previously signed defensive end Michael McCrary, an unrestricted free agent from Seattle, and used the fourth pick in last weekend's draft on Florida State defensive end Peter Boulware.
The Ravens also selected Virginia linebacker Jamie Sharper and Penn State defensive back Kim Herring in the second round of the draft.
